# RoamCat · 随心阅

> RoamCat (随心阅) is a free, open-source (MPL-2.0) browser extension for Chrome and Edge (Manifest V3) that helps Chinese-speaking readers read English websites. It has two modes on one engine: Bilingual Translation (in-place English-Chinese paragraph pairs that follow your reading position) and Reading Assistance (the page stays English; sparse hints, D+click word cards, sentence deconstruction and on-demand rescue fade as you improve). It also has a built-in PDF/EPUB reader, bilingual YouTube captions and opt-in Twitch chat translation. Local-first: no RoamCat servers, no telemetry, reading history off by default. AI comes from the user's choice — 33 bring-your-own API providers, a bundled offline MiniLM topic classifier, or a local connector reusing signed-in ChatGPT / Grok / Antigravity (Google) CLI subscriptions. UI is fully bilingual (zh/en). Status: 0.x (pre-1.0), developer-mode install, not yet on the Chrome Web Store.

Key facts (checked against the v0.7.2 source code; last updated 2026-11-01):

- Name: RoamCat is the product name and 随心阅 its Chinese name; the full name is written "RoamCat · 随心阅"
- Positioning: an open-source, local-first alternative in the bilingual-translation / reading-assistance space (compare: Immersive Translate, Relingo, 彩云小译); a rebuild of the open-source RelyLess project
- Platforms: Chrome / Edge 125+ desktop; no Firefox, Safari or mobile support
- Cost: free software; users only pay their own chosen API provider, if any
- Install: download the zip from GitHub Releases and load it unpacked in developer mode, or build from source (Node.js 22.13+); Chrome Web Store and Edge Add-ons listings are in progress
- Privacy: API keys in chrome.storage.local only; content scripts may send only 38 whitelisted message types out of 82; no remote code execution
- Tech: Manifest V3, Lit + Vite pages, lit-html content UI, Native Messaging connector (Node.js 20+), ONNX MiniLM local inference

- Next release: 14 machine-translation services with independent page, video, live-chat, reader and passage routing; optional fallback to the AI model. Chrome translation stays on device.
